__
 
• **Pyrenoids**

 
 
• Pyrenoid is a protein-rich body found in the members of Chlorophyceae or green algae. It is used for the storage of reserved food material.

• The intake of carbon dioxide and the outtake of oxygen both takes place through these pores.
 
• The respiration in leaves takes place through these tiny pores.
 
• Evaporation of water from the leaf surface occurs through the stomata.
 
• Thus, the stomata help in the process of transpiration.
 
• It also closes or opens its pores based on climatic conditions to maintain the moisture balance.
 
• It remains open during the day and closed at night. This closure at night prevents water from escaping through open pores.

• Carotenoids give the characteristic color to pumpkins, carrots, corn, tomatoes, canaries, flamingos, salmon, lobster, shrimp, and daffodils.

• Chlorophylls are porphyrins, whose molecules contain a flat ring of four-linked heterocyclic groups, based upon magnesium.
 
• Chlorophyll is a green photosynthetic pigment found in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria.

questions.question: Ferns, horsetails and lycophytes belong to which of the following groups?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pteridophyta.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ferns, horsetails, and lycophytes** all belong to the group referred to as **Pteridophyta.**
 
• These represent some of the** earlier forms of vascular plants on Earth.**
 
• They are classified as a subdivision of the plant kingdom, known as **cryptogams,** which **do not produce seeds or flowers.**
 
• Pteridophyta plants** reproduce via spores, **which are usually located on the underside of the fronds (leaves) in organs or structures called **sporangia.**
 
• The life cycle of Pteridophytes includes two distinct phases – **the large, prominent sporophyte and a less visible**, but still independent gametophyte also known as a **prothallium.**
 
• These plants are typically found in damp, shaded areas, though some have adapted to a variety of other habitats. Ferns, in particular, are known for their feather-like fronds and intricate patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bryophyta:**

 
 
• Bryophyta constitute the group of plants known as mosses and liverworts.
 
• They often grow in moist, shaded areas and are non-vascular, meaning they lack tissues for transporting water and nutrients.
 
• Unlike ferns, mosses reproduce using spores but are more primitive, often growing low to the ground.
 
 
 
• **Algae:**
 
 
• Algae is a diverse group of aquatic, photosynthetic organisms.
 
• They form a crucial part of the food chain in aquatic ecosystems and can range from microscopic sizes (microalgae) to massive kelp.
 
• Algae is not a homogeneous group but a term used to describe organisms from different evolutionary backgrounds that share some common features.
 
 
 
• **Fungi:**
 
 
• Fungi are a kingdom of usually multicellular eukaryotic organisms which are heterotrophic, meaning they obtain nutrients by consuming organic matter.
 
• They play a crucial role in nutrient cycling in ecosystems and include yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.
 
• Some fungi form symbiotic relationships with plants, aiding in nutrient absorption, while others can be pathogenic, causing diseases in plants and animals.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dinoflagellates**__.

__
 
• Gonyaulax is a genus of dinoflagellates, which are a type of plankton found in marine and freshwater environments.
 
• Dinoflagellates are characterized by their two flagella that allow them to move through the water.
 
• Many dinoflagellates, including Gonyaulax, are bioluminescent and can produce light through chemical reactions within their cells.
 
• Gonyaulax species are often associated with harmful algal blooms, sometimes referred to as "red tides," which can produce toxins harmful to marine life and humans.

• They are primarily found in freshwater environments and are known for their ability to photosynthesize using chloroplasts.
 
• Euglena is a well-known example of euglenoids.
 
 
 
• **Chrysophytes**
 
 
• Chrysophytes, also known as golden algae, are a group of algae found in both freshwater and marine environments.
 
• They have a distinctive golden-brown color due to the presence of pigments like carotenoids and xanthophylls.
 
• Chrysophytes can be unicellular or form colonies.
 
 
 
• **Protozoans**
 
 
• Protozoans are a diverse group of single-celled eukaryotic organisms that are primarily heterotrophic.
 
• They can be free-living or parasitic and are found in a variety of environments, including soil, water, and inside other organisms.
 
• Examples of protozoans include amoebas, paramecia, and plasmodia.
 
 
 
• **Dinoflagellates**
 
 
• Dinoflagellates are a group of single-celled organisms that are part of the plankton community.
 
• They possess two flagella which help in their locomotion.
 
• Some dinoflagellates are photosynthetic, while others are heterotrophic.
 
• They play a crucial role in marine ecosystems and can cause harmful algal blooms.

• **Filament**: thin hair-like structure arising from the Hook.

• Helps in locomotion
 
• Act as sensory organs (sense pH and temperature)
 
• Increase reproduction rates in few eukaryotes
 
• Used as a Secretary organelle in **Chlamydomonas**

__
 
• Chromoplasts are primarily involved in the synthesis and storage of pigments, particularly carotenoids, which give red, yellow, and orange colors to plant tissues.

• Chloroplasts, another type of plastid, contain stroma, which is a fluid matrix that houses the enzymes necessary for the synthesis of organic molecules during photosynthesis.

• These are the most well-known plastids and are responsible for photosynthesis in plant cells.

• They are involved in the synthesis and storage of starches, oils, and proteins.

• The evidence supporting this theory includes the presence of their own DNA and ribosomes within these organelles.

• It contains enzymes, ribosomes, and small circular DNA molecules.
